'''James Enderby Bidlack''' (born February 1, 1961) is an American biologist and academic. He is a professor of [[biology]] and CURE-STEM Scholar at the [[University of Central Oklahoma]], president of Metabolism Foundation<ref name=":0">{{cite web|url=http://metabolism.net/officers1.html |title=Officers |publisher=Metabolism.net |date= |access-date=2013-08-02}}</ref> and vice president of The Genome Registry.  Bidlack has co-written the textbook ''Introductory Plant Biology'' over several editions since its ninth edition.<ref name="textbook Plant biology">{{cite book |last1=Bidlack |first1=James |last2=Jansky |first2=Shelley |title=Introductory Plant Biology |date=2021 |publisher=McGraw-Hill |isbn=978-1260240832 |edition=15th |url=https://www.mheducation.com/highered/product/stern-s-introductory-plant-biology-bidlack-jansky/M9781260240832.html |access-date=22 December 2021}}</ref> He also has been involved with the [[Repository for Germinal Choice]], and appeared in a 2006 documentary about the project.<ref>{{cite journal|last=Plait |first=Phil |url=http://www.slate.com/articles/life/seed/2001/02/the_genius_babies_and_how_they_grew.html |title=The "Genius Babies," and How They Grew - Slate Magazine |journal=Slate |publisher=Slate.com |date= 8 February 2001|access-date=2013-08-02}}</ref> His work is in crop science and plant physiology, with additional involvement in biology education and genetics-related initiatives.<ref>{{cite web|last=Olding |first=Paul |url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/magazine/5078800.stm |title=UK &#124; Magazine &#124; The genius sperm bank |publisher=BBC News |date=2006-06-15 |access-date=2013-08-02}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Bidlack was born in [[Minneapolis, Minnesota]], the youngest son of Verne C. and Norma L. Bidlack. His father, Verne C. Bidlack, Jr., contributed to the Manhattan Project during [[World War II]].<ref>https://www.metabolism.net/bidlack/family/familypics/geneaology/Dad%20Certificate%20Manhattan%20Project.jpg U.S. War Department - Army Service Forces - Corps of Engineers - Manhattan District - Production of the Atomic Bomb - Verne C. Bidlack, Jr. (Chrysler Corporation) Appreciation Certificate (6 August 1945)</ref> 

He earned a [[Bachelor of Science]] degree in soil and crop science from [[Purdue University]] in 1984. He completed a Master of Science in [[crop physiology]] at the [[University of Arkansas]] in 1986 under Charles A. Stutte.<ref>{{Cite web |title=UCO: James Bidlack, Ph.D. |url=https://www3.uco.edu/centraldirectory/profiles/2120 |access-date=2026-04-14 |website=www3.uco.edu}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Central Oklahoma Professor Awarded Three Grants |url=https://www.oklahoman.com/story/news/1991/07/17/central-oklahoma-professor-awarded-three-grants/62522364007/ |access-date=2026-04-14 |website=The Oklahoman |language=en-US}}</ref>

He received a Ph.D. in plant physiology from [[Iowa State University]] in 1990 under Dwayne R. Buxton and Richard M. Shibles. His doctoral dissertation, ''Cell Wall Components and Lignin Biosynthesis in Forages'', examined structural and biochemical aspects of plant cell walls.<ref>{{cite thesis|last=Bidlack|first=James Enderby|title=Cell Wall Components and Lignin Biosynthesis in Forages|type=PhD thesis|publisher=Iowa State University|url=https://dr.lib.iastate.edu/server/api/core/bitstreams/bed7ed72-bba0-4885-8e50-75de9190ddb9/content}}</ref>

==Career==
After completing his doctoral studies, Bidlack joined the [[University of Central Oklahoma]] as a faculty member.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Outstanding Alumni Awards |url=https://crop-soil-environmental-sciences.uark.edu/ |access-date=2026-04-14 |website=Crop, Soil, and Environmental Sciences |language=en}}</ref>

At the University of Central Oklahoma, he was hired as an [[assistant professor]] in 1990, promoted to associate professor in 1998, and to full professor in 2002.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |date=2019-05-03 |title=UCO Biology Professor Recognized for Contributions to Multimedia Resources for Teachers Worldwide |url=https://www3.uco.edu/press/prdetail.asp?NewsID=26332 |access-date=2026-04-14 |website=www3.uco.edu |language=en-US}}</ref>

His research has included work in crop science and plant physiology.  His earlier studies examined weed control in pigeon pea and nitrogen content and biomass in legume crop rotations.<ref name="sciencedirect">{{cite journal |doi=10.1016/j.fcr.2005.05.005 |title=Weed control in a pigeon pea–wheat cropping system |year=2006 |last1=Bidlack |first1=James E. |last2=Middick |first2=Andy |last3=Shantz |first3=Delmar |last4=MacKown |first4=Charles T. |last5=Williams |first5=Robert D. |last6=Rao |first6=Srinivas C. |journal=Field Crops Research |volume=96 |page=63|url=https://naldc-legacy.nal.usda.gov/naldc/download.xhtml?id=21004&content=PDF |url-access=subscription }}{{dead link|date=June 2025|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> Later work investigated pigeon pea morphology and physiological responses to water stress.<ref>{{cite journal |doi=10.1080/00103624.2011.605491 |title=Morphology, Biomass, and Vessel Diameter of Pigeon Pea Subjected to Water Stress |year=2011 |last1=Porter |first1=Monty A. |last2=Bidlack |first2=James E. |journal=Communications in Soil Science and Plant Analysis |volume=42 |issue=19 |page=2334|bibcode=2011CSSPA..42.2334P |s2cid=83774807 }}</ref> He has also co-authored research on a type IV secretion system in ''Escherichia coli'' that increases sensitivity to bile salts.<ref>{{cite journal |doi=10.1128/JB.186.16.5202-5209.2004 |title=An Active Type IV Secretion System Encoded by the F Plasmid Sensitizes Escherichia coli to Bile Salts |year=2004 |last1=Bidlack |first1=J. E. |last2=Silverman |first2=P. M. |journal=Journal of Bacteriology |volume=186 |issue=16 |pages=5202–9 |pmid=15292121 |pmc=490876}}</ref>

Bidlack serves as president of the Metabolism Foundation and vice president of the Genome Registry. He has also participated in academic and educational service activities, including contributions to biology education initiatives and professional organizations.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://oklahoman.com/article/3903672/name-that-gene-genome-registry-offers-opportunity-to-pay-for-pseudonym|work=The Oklahoman|title= Name that gene: Genome Registry offers opportunity to pay for pseudonym |last=Marks|first=Jay F.|date=November 11, 2021|access-date=December 22, 2021}}</ref>

Bidlack participated in a 2006 documentary discussing the ''Repository for Germinal Choice''.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2006-06-15 |title=The genius sperm bank |url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/magazine/5078800.stm |access-date=2026-04-14 |language=en-GB}}</ref>

Bidlack is a co-author of the textbook ''Introductory Plant Biology'', also published as ''Stern’s Introductory Plant Biology.''<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" />
